solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lie next to reptile, we hear: one's got too close!

indicators.note: next to places one sound directly beside the other, the lie first
we hear says the words before it count only for how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a lie is a tale, a made-up story
a gator is an alligator, informally

explanation.surface: A spoken warning about a lizard lying beside someone who has crept up far too close.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, TALE GATOR is TAILGATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailgater is a driver following another vehicle much too closely behind.

clue.text: Retiring from magazine, largely to go on papers?

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the last letter of the magazine is dropped
to go on means the first piece is put down ahead of the next one

parts.note: Time is a well-known news magazine
identity papers, ID

explanation.surface: Someone stepping back from a magazine job to work mostly on newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiring person is shy and reserved, avoiding attention, which is what being timid means.

clue.text: Islamic prophet left departing sign that man must follow

indicators.note: must follow puts that man after the shortened sign
departing tells us that the letter for left goes away from the sign

parts.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac
L is the usual abbreviation for left
a pronoun for a male person already mentioned

explanation.surface: A star sign losing a letter while a man trails behind sounds like an astrology puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibrahim is the Arabic form of Abraham, revered as a prophet in Islam.

clue.text: Finally reach bypass: closed! …

parts.note: to bypass an obstacle is to get round it
a door that is to is shut

explanation.surface: A motorist at last arrives at a bypass, only to find it shut.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue on into 4 down, but each is solved alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To get around to a task is at last to deal with it after a delay.

clue.text: … furthermore has got directed to visit Spanish city

indicators.note: has got means the first word holds the second within it

parts.note: too means also, furthermore
led as in guided or directed

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: someone has also been told to go and see a city in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic city in central Spain, famous for its swords and its cathedral.

clue.text: Recording of note: good first track

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
G is the abbreviation for good
1st, with the numeral read as the letter I
RY is short for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A music reviewer praises a recording whose opening track is good.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Recording' a record, but it is the act of entering something in an official record.
explanation.definitionFit: Registry can mean registration, the formal entering of details in an official list.

clue.text: Port that's cheap is flat — oddly left out

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are omitted, so only the even ones remain

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of these words

explanation.surface: An estate agent's dismissive verdict on a port town's cheap apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Haifa is a major seaport on Israel's Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: One foolishly talked through part of speech — a travesty!

indicators.note: part of says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: spanning the end of speech and the start of travesty

explanation.surface: A listener scorns a speech in which someone talked nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk through your hat is an idiom for speaking ignorant nonsense, so this item is what the fool talked through.

clue.text: Broadcaster's prompt expected soon?

indicators.note: a broadcaster speaks over the air, so we take the sound of the next word

parts.note: to prompt someone to act is to incite them

explanation.surface: A newsreader's autocue cue suggests something is coming up shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in sight is close at hand and can be expected before long, like an end in view.

clue.text: Any diary entry for August? Not normally — save for this?

definitions.note: the whole phrase is the idiom 'save for a rainy day', with this standing for the answer

indicators.note: not in the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the entry to a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of August

explanation.surface: Remarking that August diary entries are rarely about wet weather, in a British summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saving for a rainy day is an idiom for putting money aside against future hardship.

clue.text: Fighting to promote one connected with union

indicators.note: promoting one means lifting it out of its place and setting it back in higher up the word

parts.note: martial means relating to fighting or war
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fighting force advancing one member who is linked with the trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: In MARTIAL the I moves two places earlier, giving MARITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital means relating to marriage, the union of husband and wife.

clue.text: Were all given share of lifebelts, apparently, to join navy

parts.note: were given means got
a lifebelt is a ring, shaped like the letter O
a share for all is one each, abbreviated EA

explanation.surface: New recruits are each handed a lifebelt as they sign up for the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as GOT O'S, EA: everyone got rings, one each.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to sea is to become a sailor, which is what joining the navy amounts to.

clue.text: I shouldn't have done that first degree

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the exclamation made on realising a silly mistake
second meaning: the first note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.walkthrough: First degree sounds like a criminal charge or a university award, but it is the keynote of a musical scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer Simpson's cry of self-reproach is spelt the same as the opening note of the sol-fa scale.

clue.text: Are armed guards urged on this recklessly?

definitions.note: a plural verb phrase; the answer is the base form of the verb

indicators.note: done recklessly, without care, so the letters fall into a wild new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether security guards are being pushed into rash action.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding shotgun originally meant sitting beside a stagecoach driver carrying a gun as protection.

clue.text: Catching up with court case

parts.note: when time is up, it is over
a hearing is a session of a court case

explanation.surface: Someone getting up to date with a trial in the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhearing is chancing to hear talk not meant for you, so catching words by accident.

clue.text: Raise, or rear, young animal

parts.note: the rear, or backside; bum is British slang for bottom
a pup is a young dog or seal

explanation.surface: Choosing whether to bring up a young animal, phrased as a rearing question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise, or rear' looks like a pair of synonyms for the definition, but rear supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump up a price or rating is informally to increase it.

clue.text: Conduct a sextet: take some minutes about it

indicators.note: the phrase about the sextet goes round it, enclosing it

parts.note: to take some minutes is to last, say to be an hour
taken as written
the Roman numeral for six

explanation.surface: Instructions to lead a six-piece ensemble, allowing it some time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conduct a sextet' looks like a musician's job; conduct is the noun meaning how one acts.
explanation.definitionFit: Conduct as a noun is the way someone acts, which is a synonym of how they behave.

clue.text: Run in second of marathons? Trot maybe around the others?

indicators.note: second of picks out the second letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the second letter of marathons

indicators.note: around means the Trot surrounds the others

parts.note: a Trot, a Trotskyist, is an example of a Red, a left-winger
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A runner in a marathon wonders whether jogging round the rest of the field counts.
explanation.walkthrough: Run in is slang for arrested; Trot is short for Trotskyist, not a gentle jog.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone in is informal for taking them into police custody, so arrested is past participle.

clue.text: Profiting from popular compact

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
pocket means small, as in a pocket edition

explanation.surface: Someone making money out of a fashionable cosmetic compact.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone who comes out ahead financially, with more cash than before, is said to be in pocket.

clue.text: Where the bills are piling up

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large board for posters, a billboard
second meaning: amassing and storing things away

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as unpaid bills stacking up, but the bills are posters on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarding is a British advertising board on which posters are stuck, and hoarding also means stockpiling.

clue.text: Rascal, one defended in part by curate?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rogue, a disreputable person

definitions.text: one defended in part by curate?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the rotten breakfast item a timid curate said was good in parts

explanation.walkthrough: A famous 1895 Punch cartoon shows a curate served a spoiled egg by his bishop, insisting that parts of it are excellent; hence a curate's egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a thoroughly worthless person after a spoiled egg, and the curate's egg was exactly such a spoiled one.

clue.text: Maybe make of fool of Yankee that's drunk

parts.note: a fool is a whipped fruit dessert, made perhaps by beating with a whisk
Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Making a fool of an intoxicated American.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool here is a British pudding of fruit folded into whipped cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky is a spirit, something that is drunk, in the sense of being swallowed.

clue.text: Performer viewed with pride, possibly, a rising talent

parts.note: pride is one of the seven deadly sins
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a talent or skill is an art

explanation.surface: A proud audience watches a young performer on the way up.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was a celebrated American singer and actor, so a performer.

clue.text: German commander is gracious, reflecting about French wife?

indicators.note: about means going round the French wife
a reflection shows things back to front, so the word is turned round

parts.note: Lor! is an exclamation of surprise, like Gracious!
Mme, Madame, is the French title for a married woman

explanation.surface: A general's kindness reflecting on the French woman he married.
explanation.definitionFit: Erwin Rommel was a German field marshal of the Second World War, the Desert Fox.

clue.text: Cross road, or also avoid, somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to a pedestrian: cross the road, or else find some way to dodge it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross road' looks like an instruction; it is the road of the Cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The Via Dolorosa in Jerusalem is the route Jesus is believed to have walked carrying his cross.

clue.text: The present Dawn has to give Dan

parts.note: what the name Dawn must lose to become another name: it must have none of one letter
the letter in Dawn that is absent from Dan

explanation.surface: A present-giving exchange: Dawn is obliged to hand a gift to Dan.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike the W from Dawn and you get Dan, so Dawn must have NO W.
explanation.definitionFit: Now is the present moment, this time rather than past or future.

clue.text: Secure chain for lifting equipment

parts.note: to secure a prize is to win it
CH is the abbreviation for chain, an old unit of length

explanation.surface: Fastening a chain to the hoisting gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A winch is a drum-and-cable device used for hauling or hoisting heavy loads.

clue.text: King standing after he passed on priest's dagger

indicators.note: standing after means the king is placed behind the other pieces

parts.note: ob, for Latin obiit, means he died, as on gravestones
Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king stands over a dead priest's dagger, a murder-mystery tableau.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dagger' looks like a weapon; it is the printer's mark † used for footnotes or deaths.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelisk is the typographical dagger sign, a printer's mark used for footnote references.

clue.text: Pub popular when granted extension?

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
the word is extended by repeating its final letter

explanation.surface: A bar becomes busy once allowed to stay open late.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a pub granted an extension may serve drinks past the usual closing time.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a public house, a place serving drink and often lodging to travellers.

clue.text: Precursor to deluge, it was said, gun getting damp

parts.words: Precursor to deluge, it was said
parts.note: Louis XV supposedly said Après moi, le déluge: after me, the flood
the Sten was a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A rain forecast says a gun will get wet before the flood.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to damp something is to make it slightly wet, a synonym for moisten.

clue.text: President's earlier a failing, ungrateful character

indicators.note: earlier specifies which of two identical letters in the name is the one that goes
failing means going missing, so a letter is lost from the name

parts.note: Ronald Reagan, US president 1981 to 1989
taken as written

explanation.surface: A president's past shortcoming, seen as ingratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters, who repays her father's gift of his kingdom with cruelty.

clue.text: Signal for one to knock hard after ring?

indicators.note: after means what precedes it in the clue comes later than ring

parts.note: to ring is to telephone, abbreviated TEL
e.g., for example, for one
a rap is a sharp knock
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A doorbell rings, and the visitor then knocks loudly as a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To telegraph is to signal or make obvious in advance, as a boxer telegraphs a punch.
